s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive swelling of the forearm with a firm, non-tender mass and cortical bone irregularity
salient_findings: Progressively enlarging swelling on the posterior ulnar aspect of the forearm
Firm, non-tender 4 × 5 cm mass in the subcutaneous tissues
Cortical irregularity of the adjacent ulna on radiographs
Mass arising from the bone and extending into the soft tissues on MRI
key_facts: No family history of similar lesions
Normal neurovascular examination of the hand
Soft-tissue swelling with cortical irregularity on radiographs
Mass isointense to muscle on T1-weighted MRI
Cortical bone lysis with medullary involvement

shortlist.label: Osteosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Aggressive bone lesion with cortical bone lysis and medullary involvement

shortlist.label: Ewing's sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Bone tumor with soft tissue extension and aggressive features

shortlist.label: Chondrosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Cartilaginous tumor with potential for cortical bone destruction

shortlist.label: Adamantinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Rare bone tumor with potential for cortical bone lysis and soft tissue extension

shortlist.label: Osteofibrous dysplasia
shortlist.why_kept: Benign fibro-osseous lesion with potential for cortical bone irregularity

raw.rationale: The presence of cortical bone lysis with medullary involvement and a mass that is isointense to muscle on T1-weighted images and heterogeneous hyperintense on T2-weighted images with marked enhancement after gadolinium administration are consistent with osteosarcoma, a primary malignant bone tumor.

rejected.label: Ewing's sarcoma
rejected.why: While Ewing's sarcoma can also present with bone lysis and a soft tissue mass, it typically occurs in younger patients and has a more aggressive clinical course.

rejected.label: Chondrosarcoma
rejected.why: Chondrosarcoma is more common in older adults and typically presents with a cartilaginous matrix on imaging, which is not described in this case.

rejected.label: Adamantinoma
rejected.why: Adamantinoma is a rare tumor that typically occurs in the tibia and has a distinct radiographic appearance with multiple cortical holes and a 'soap bubble' appearance, not seen in this case.

rejected.label: Osteofibrous dysplasia
rejected.why: Osteofibrous dysplasia is a benign fibro-osseous lesion that typically presents with a well-defined cortical defect and does not exhibit the aggressive features seen in this case, such as cortical bone lysis and a large soft tissue mass.
